split_question: When a big high street chain is failing, should the government step in to keep its stores open?
angles: pay and retrain the workers, let the stores go
back a rescue to keep stores and jobs open
help the towns first: reuse the empty shops
facts_for_writers: Dismissed employees of a failed chain can claim statutory redundancy pay and notice pay from the Insolvency Service, which says it tries to pay eligible claims within 6 weeks (Wilko case, 2023). [s3]
Workers and self-employed contractors, as opposed to employees, cannot make that claim and must register as creditors with the administrators instead. [s4]

You are normally entitled to statutory redundancy pay if you have worked for your employer for 2 years or more; for redundancies from 6 April 2026 weekly pay is capped at £751 and the maximum is £22,530. [s5]
If whole-company bids for Poundland fail, its stores, staff and stock could be auctioned to rivals such as Tesco, B&M and Lidl. [s1]
The Business Secretary has said he is keeping his options for intervention in the Poundland case "under review". [s2]
